_note: v5.6: exploratory probe, NOT trained. v5.5's learned crop/disease vectors and LoRA adapters, unchanged, scored with zero-shot v3.6's prompt text (each pair's embedding = renormalised mean of a taxonomy sentence and a symptom sentence) instead of the symptom-only sentence they were trained in. Run by train/prompt_swap.py. No validation model exists for the new text, so gamma is v5.5's (0.075, chosen for the old prompts) and the result is a test probe, not a selected version; v5.7 is the properly trained version of the same idea (val 55.6% vs v5.5's 56.9%).
_result: Worse than v5.5: swapping in v3.6's two-sentence text without retraining hurts. With v5.5's gamma 0.075: seen 47.3% (v5.5 52.2%), unseen 87.9% (v5.5 84.3%), HM 61.5% top-1 / 91.7% top-5 (v5.5 64.5% / 92.1%). The shift toward unseen is partly the borrowed gamma being wrong for the new text, but even each one's best TEST gamma (diagnostic only) gives the same verdict: 67.0% vs v5.5's 67.2%. Uncalibrated (gamma 0) it is clearly worse: HM 32.2% vs 40.3%, unseen disease 25.6% vs 32.3%. As expected, the learned vectors only work in the sentence they were trained in; v5.7 (trained with both sentences) is the fair test of the idea and also did not beat v5.5.
title: prompt_swap

model._note: Same OpenAI CLIP ViT-B/16 (QuickGELU) as v4.1/v4.2; the text encoder stays frozen.

image_encoder._note: From v5.3: v5 + more LoRA capacity: last 8 blocks instead of 4, rank 16 instead of 8. alpha 16 -> 32 keeps the LoRA scale (alpha/rank) at 2, so only capacity changes, not the effective step size. About 4x more adapter parameters (1.57M vs 393k). Same lr.

input._note: Images come from the 256 px resize cache (runs/cache/resized_256, shared with the CNN baselines). Test: CLIP's resize 224 + centre crop + CLIP mean/std. The app must standardise uploads the same way (dpd/resize_cache.standardise).

augmentation._note: Same as the CNN baselines except a milder crop scale (0.5-1 instead of 0.25-1), because CLIP's pretrained features expect whole-object views. No hue jitter: colour is diagnostic.

prompts._note: v5.5's templates with v3.6's [taxonomy, visual] description lists (same file as v5.7).

validation._note: Same procedure as v4.2 but 1 split instead of 3: each split is now a full training run with the image encoder in the loop (images instead of cached embeddings). Note v4.2 showed one split can mis-set gamma, so treat v5's gamma with that caveat.

training._note: Prompt vectors as v4.2 (AdamW lr 2e-4, weight decay 0, logit scale 100, loss weights pair 1 / crop 0.5 / disease 0.5). max_epochs 30 -> 15 (v4.1/v4.2 selected epochs 13-18 with cached features; each epoch now re-encodes every image). Batch 256 -> 64 for GPU memory with gradients through 4 image-encoder blocks.

runtime._note: Gradient checkpointing on the text encoder as before. 4 dataloader workers read the resize cache.

prompt_swap._note: Source run whose vectors and adapters are reused.
